hints.title: Uniform Chunk Window Inspection
hints.text: Because all words have the same uniform length, slice the input string into fixed-size chunks of that word length.

hints.title: Offset-Based Segment Alignments
hints.text: Run separate scans for each possible starting remainder modulo word length to cover every possible word boundary alignment.

hints.title: Word Frequency Window Tracking
hints.text: For each offset from zero to word length minus one, slide a window by word length chunks. Maintain a count of matching words. When a word exceeds its expected frequency or an unknown word appears, shrink the window from the left until counts are valid.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def findSubstring(self, s: str, words: List[str]) -> List[int]:
        if not s or not words:
            return []
        word_len = len(words[0])
        word_count = len(words)
        total_len = word_len * word_count
        word_freq = Counter(words)
        res = []

        for i in range(word_len):
            left = i
            curr_map = Counter()
            count = 0
            for j in range(i, len(s) - word_len + 1, word_len):
                sub = s[j:j + word_len]
                if sub in word_freq:
                    curr_map[sub] += 1
                    count += 1
                    while curr_map[sub] > word_freq[sub]:
                        curr_map[s[left:left + word_len]] -= 1
                        count -= 1
                        left += word_len
                    if count == word_count:
                        res.append(left)
                else:
                    curr_map.clear()
                    count = 0
                    left = j + word_len
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal sliding window shifting across L distinct modular offsets.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rechecking every position from scratch takes O(N * M * L) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sliding window per modular offset maintains word counts in O(N) aggregate steps.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Decompose the string by starting offset mod word length to reuse adjacent chunk computations.
